## Summary

There is a high severity authentication vulnerability in Traefik's ForwardAuth middleware when the authentication server uses a connection-bound scheme such as NTLM or SPNEGO/Kerberos "Negotiate". The fix for GHSA-hrpp-p4fc-wwf8 sends the subrequests of a client that presents such a credential on a dedicated connection to the authentication server, but it only detects the credential in the `Authorization` header. ForwardAuth also forwards the `Proxy-Authorization` header, and a credential sent in that header still goes through the connection pool shared by every client. An unauthenticated client can then reuse an authentication-server connection already authenticated by another user, receive that user's identity through `authResponseHeaders`, and access the backend as that user. The patched versions apply the same isolation to `Proxy-Authorization`.

Traefik v3.0 through v3.6 are end-of-life and are also affected; they will not receive a fix on their own line. As a workaround, set `authRequestHeaders` to a list that does not include `Proxy-Authorization`.

## Patches

- https://github.com/traefik/traefik/releases/tag/v2.11.62
